sourceProfile.notes: Wire facts taken from the OpenAPI 3.1 fragments embedded in each nango.dev/docs reference page (fetched as raw markdown) plus the auth, webhook and Zero YAML guides. The documented API document version string is 'Nango API 1.0.0'; individual endpoints are not separately versioned and the paths carry no version prefix.
verified: POST /connect/sessions -> 201 { data: { token, expires_at, connect_link? } }; body fields tags (<=10 keys, values <=255 chars, keys lowercased), allowed_integrations, integrations_config_defaults, overrides, webhook_url_override; end_user and organization are marked deprecated in favour of tags; session lifetime documented as 30 minutes; requires environment:connect_sessions:write

POST /connect/sessions/reconnect -> 201 same ConnectSession envelope; required body connection_id + integration_id; documented restriction: only connections created with a connect session are compatible
GET /integrations -> 200 { data: Integration[] } with unique_key, display_name, provider, logo, created_at, updated_at, forward_webhooks; no pagination parameters documented
GET /integrations/{uniqueKey} -> 200 { data: IntegrationFull }; include=webhook|credentials query controls disclosure of webhook_url and client credentials

GET /integrations/{uniqueKey}/functions -> 200 { data: ListedNangoFunction[], pagination: { total, page, limit } }; page default 0, limit default 20 max 100; type filter sync|action|on-event; sync rows carry runs, auto_start, track_deletes; all rows carry id, enabled, last_deployed, source

GET /connections -> 200 { connections: [...] } explicitly 'without credentials'; filters connectionId, search, tags[key] (deepObject), limit, page; endUserId/endUserOrganizationId deprecated in favour of tag filtering

GET /connections/{connectionId}?provider_config_key=... -> 200 ConnectionFull WITH credentials; documented side effect: 'Every time you fetch the connection with this API endpoint, Nango will check if the access token has expired. If it has, it will refresh it.'; force_refresh and refresh_token query flags (both default false); 424 documented as 'Connection refresh exhausted'
DELETE /connections/{connectionId}?provider_config_key=... -> 200 { success }
PATCH /connections/{connectionId} accepts webhook_url_override (empty string clears it)

{GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE} /proxy/{anyPath}: required headers Connection-Id and Provider-Config-Key; optional Retries, Retry-On, Base-Url-Override, Decompress, nango-proxy-$ANY_HEADER; upstream status, headers and body passed through verbatim

POST /action/trigger: required headers Connection-Id and Provider-Config-Key; body { action_name, input }; optional X-Async and X-Max-Retries (0-5); async response { id, statusUrl }; documented errors 400, 424 (action http error) and 500 (action error)

POST /sync/trigger, /sync/start, /sync/pause -> 200 { success }; body provider_config_key + syncs (names or {name, variant}); connection_id optional and, when omitted, applies to ALL relevant connections; /sync/trigger opts.reset and opts.emptyCache clear checkpoints and the record cache

GET /sync/status -> 200 { syncs: [...] } with id, connection_id, name, variant, status (RUNNING|PAUSED|STOPPED|SUCCESS|ERROR), finishedAt, nextScheduledSyncAt, frequency, latestResult, recordCount, checkpoint; syncs parameter required, '*' means all, variants use syncName::variantName

GET /records: required headers Connection-Id and Provider-Config-Key; query model (required), cursor, limit, filter, modified_after, ids, variant; delta deprecated in favour of modified_after; records carry _nango_metadata { deleted_at, last_action, first_seen_at, last_modified_at, cursor, pruned_at } and the page carries next_cursor

Webhook signature: header X-Nango-Hmac-Sha256 is an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with the environment webhook signing key (hex). The docs explicitly warn that the legacy X-Nango-Signature header uses plain SHA-256, is sent only for backwards compatibility and 'should not be used'; the signing key is distinct from the Environment API key

Webhook types: auth (operations creation, override, refresh, deletion; fields connectionId, providerConfigKey, provider, authMode, environment, success, tags, error), sync (syncName, model, success, modifiedAfter, responseResults{added,updated,deleted}, checkpoints{from,to} which may be missing or null, deprecated syncType), forward ({ from, type, connectionId, providerConfigKey, payload }, with unattributed events forwarded as the raw provider payload)

Webhook delivery: retried twice with exponential backoff on non-2xx, 20 second timeout; webhook_url_override replaces (does not add to) the environment's primary and secondary URLs and is settable only by a trusted actor - a webhook_url passed to nango.auth() params from the client is explicitly ignored

Authentication: 'Authorization: Bearer <NANGO-API-KEY>'; Environment vs Account API keys are not interchangeable; missing scope yields 403; error bodies follow StdError { error: { code, message?, errors? } }
Rate limits: 429 with Retry-After; X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset on every response

Zero YAML: nango.yaml is deprecated; syncs/actions/on-event functions are defined in TypeScript via createSync/createAction/createOnEvent and their deployed metadata is served by the functions endpoints above (no YAML parser is needed)
unverified: Whether GET /integrations paginates for large environments: the reference page documents no pagination parameters, so the adapter pages the already-returned array client-side and records the limitation

The exact upstream behaviour when a reconnect session is created for a connection that was not created through a connect session: the restriction is documented in prose but no specific error code is published

Asynchronous action polling (GET of the returned statusUrl) is documented only as a path template on the action page; no response schema is published, so the adapter does not use X-Async and treats an unexpected async envelope as indeterminate
No endpoint is documented for revoking a provider grant upstream, and none for cancelling an in-flight sync run (only pause); both are reported as native limitations rather than approximated

limitations: GET /integrations documents no pagination parameters; the adapter pages the returned array client-side with an opaque cursor that carries its own page size.
Integration client credentials are never requested (include=credentials is never sent), so discovery cannot report OAuth client ids or scopes configured in Nango.

Per-integration auth requirements are reported as the two external-broker profiles plus the function metadata Nango exposes; Nango does not publish a per-integration auth-mode field on these endpoints.
workItems.notes: Identity is environment + API origin (authorityNamespace) plus unique_key; the provider slug is only a display/grouping key, so two GitHub integrations in one environment stay distinct directory rows grouped under one service. Native capability metadata (sync runs/auto_start/track_deletes, action schemas, on-event events, enabled/last_deployed/source) is carried through as inert nativeExtensions.

limitations: A connect session alone proves only that Nango holds a connection for the bound integration. Exact-account intents require an approved read-only verification operation in the binding; without one an exact-account intent is denied rather than relabelled verified (AC-AUTH-08).
Reconnect completion needs either an HMAC-verified auth/override webhook or a prior auth error that clears in GET /connections; Nango publishes no reconnect-specific server state to poll.
The connect_link is accepted only when its origin equals the approved connect destination.
workItems.notes: allowed_integrations is always exactly the one integration the binding names. Tags are derived from the authenticated actor through the host owner mapping and are digests, never raw subject ids; the deprecated end_user/organization inputs are never sent. token, expires_at and connect_link go only to HandoffIssue.private, and the session expiry is bounded by the documented 30-minute ceiling. webhook_url_override is default-deny: only an administrator-approved destination recorded in binding settings can set it, and the strict intent schema rejects any caller-supplied attempt.

limitations: Reading this endpoint can refresh the upstream token as a documented side effect; the adapter cannot make it side-effect free, so it records refreshMayHaveOccurred: true on every inspection and serialises the call through the custody port's single-flight refresh.
Bounded metadata only: metadata deeper or larger than the configured bounds is dropped and reported as metadataOmitted rather than stored.
workItems.notes: inspectConnection is exposed on the provider-specific NangoAdapter type, not on ConnectorAdapter, so a generic read-only agent route cannot dispatch it; agent actors are refused outright. The response passes through a strict allowlist (connection_id, provider_config_key, provider, created_at, updated_at, last_fetched_at, tags, metadata, errors) plus only the credential scheme and expiry; access and refresh tokens and the raw provider block never leave the parser and the stored broker reference is never replaced by a token. force_refresh=false and refresh_token=false are sent explicitly.

limitations: Base-Url-Override, Retries, Retry-On and Decompress are never sent from caller input; Retries is set only from the approved contract and only for read-only operations.
X-Async is not used: the async action result schema is not published, so an unexpected async envelope is treated as indeterminate rather than parsed.
A 5xx from Nango on a non-read operation whose replay policy is 'none' is reported indeterminate, because Nango may already have forwarded the request upstream.
workItems.notes: Provider-Config-Key and Connection-Id come only from the connection's protected broker reference, which is re-checked against the stored credential material inside credentials.use. Operations are BoundOperations with explicit destination, path template, input/output subset schemas, deadline, response ceiling, per-connection rate limit and retry budget. An input carrying baseUrlOverride, headers, connection_id, provider_config_key, action_name, retries or credentials is refused with nango.input.override-rejected before any credential is touched. Action names come only from the BoundOperation.

limitations: Nango documents no endpoint to cancel a running sync execution; 'cancel' maps to POST /sync/pause (pausing the schedule) and the result says so explicitly via nango.sync.cancel-maps-to-pause.
opts.reset and opts.emptyCache are refused: they clear Nango's checkpoints and record cache, which is a data-destroying operation this adapter does not expose.
Sync execution, scheduling and checkpointing remain Nango's; nothing here reimplements them.
workItems.notes: Every sync command carries an explicit connection_id, because Nango applies a command to all relevant connections when it is omitted. Status rows (including Nango's own checkpoint object) are passed through verbatim. Records are read through GET /records with cursor/modified_after. Function metadata comes from the API, never from nango.yaml, which import refuses with a blocking diagnostic.

limitations: The legacy X-Nango-Signature header is ignored even when correct, per the documentation's own guidance; NANGO_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY is required for the events dimension and the Environment API key is never used as a fallback.

No shared event inbox was available from the EVENT swarm at implementation time, so dedupe uses a bounded in-process inbox (authority-scoped, 4096 entries, 1 hour window). The adapter accepts an injected inbox through NangoAdapterOptions.eventInbox and the integrator should supply the durable one.
Nango documents no upstream grant revocation endpoint, so revoke reports 'unsupported' rather than deleting the broker connection and calling it revocation.
workItems.notes: X-Nango-Hmac-Sha256 is verified in constant time over the exact raw bytes before parsing; bodies are bounded and prototype-polluting keys refused. Auth webhooks map to lifecycle only after re-reading GET /connections, so a replayed deletion cannot unbind a live connection and a transient refresh failure Nango already recovered is degraded rather than reconnect-required. Local unlink is the default disconnect; DELETE /connections/{id} runs only under scope 'broker', and a shared Nango connection referenced by another local connection blocks it until an administrator approves the shared impact.

integrationPatches.description: Register createNangoAdapter(options) from src/server/connectors/providers/nango/index.ts. Signature: createNangoAdapter(options?: NangoAdapterOptions): NangoAdapter, where NangoAdapter extends ConnectorAdapter with the privileged-internal methods inspectConnection, reconcileEvent, deleteBrokerConnection, captureIntegration and catalogEntries. Adapter id 'nango', ecosystem 'nango', service 'nango', runtime hosted-server, support provider-backed, custody [external-credential-broker, external-execution-broker]. The base adapter's service key is 'nango'; per-integration directory rows come from adapter.catalogEntries(ctx, present), which needs a call context because it reads the Nango API.

Supply ownerMapping (authenticated actor -> owner id / organization id per host policy; the default maps only ownerKind 'user' to the subject and refuses organization and workload), resolveConnection (tenant + authorityInstance + providerConfigKey + connectionId -> local connectionRef, used to attribute non-creation webhooks), sharedReferences (other local connections referencing the same Nango connection id, which gates broker deletion) and eventInbox (the durable authority-scoped dedupe inbox once the EVENT swarm's inbox exists).

NANGO_SECRET_KEY (secret, required), NANGO_ENVIRONMENT (public, required; lowercase token such as prod or dev), NANGO_HOST (public, optional, self-hosted API origin which must equal the approved 'api' destination origin) and NANGO_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY (secret, optional but required for the events dimension; distinct from the API key).

Every Nango binding needs destination id 'api' (default https://api.nango.dev, or the NANGO_HOST origin) and, for connect/reconnect, destination id 'connect' (default https://connect.nango.dev). The helper nangoDestinations({ apiOrigin?, connectOrigin?, network? }) from providers/nango/index.ts builds both. Binding.settings must parse against nangoBindingSettingsSchema: integration { uniqueKey, provider }, presentation, optional administrator-approved webhookUrlOverride, optional verification { operationRef, identityPointer, targetKind } and per-operation contracts keyed by operationRef.

Mount a POST route (suggested /api/v1/connectors/nango/events) that reads the RAW body bytes before any JSON parsing, calls adapter.events.verify(ctx, { headers, body, receivedAt }) and, on a verified envelope, calls adapter.reconcileEvent(ctx, event) to obtain { duplicate, ordering, code, lifecycle?, adapterState?, syncStatus? } and persists lifecycle/adapterState through the connection store. Verification returns undefined for anything unverifiable, which must be answered without disclosing why. Auth webhooks with operation 'creation' complete a pending handoff through adapter.complete(ctx, { kind: 'event', event }) instead.
